entry.title: Research Summary: November 28, 2026
entry.summary: This cycle's research/documentation coverage is dominated by Hermes Agent ecosystem activity, led by a serious supply-chain security incident: a malicious NPM package (leadstack-crm-connect) backdoored victim machines by installing Hermes Agent as root and tasking it via Telegram — making it the top item given direct, high-impact relevance to anyone running the agent. Official changes follow: new support for Claude Pro/Max subscription authentication (lowering access barriers) and official Kanban multi-agent collaboration docs addressing coordination pain. Deployment and infrastructure remains a strong theme with actionable gaps documented — no official Helm chart, root-at-init container requirements complicating hardened Kubernetes deploys — plus practical community guides for containerized setups and VPS-to-rooted-Android control patterns. Community tooling is flourishing: Comemo (composite memory provider fanning out writes past the single-provider limitation), Refine Cycle (self-improvement plugin), Hermes-Voice (Home Assistant integration), Paper Harness (native SwiftUI iPhone client), ClusterMob (profile registry), and lighter-weight orchestrators (shoebox, Verso) that double as friction signals against growing complexity. Performance practitioners report custom Metal kernels replacing MLX for dramatic local-inference gains on Mac clusters. Multi-agent orchestration demand is a recurring theme across Ask HN threads and third-party tools. Academic research items (context engineering, evidence-grounded 3D agentic reasoning, AIChipbench for accelerator-design agents) are conceptually adjacent but lack direct implementation ties and rank lower. Excluded: three Black Friday SEO/backlink promotional posts with zero technical or documentation relevance. One minor note: a thread references "GLM 5.3 Flash," which does not match current Zhipu/Z.ai model listings (latest GLM is 5.2) — likely a version typo in the post and not a model-release claim.

entry.title: Tell HN: Stop using MLX, start telling your agent to write custom kernels

entry.title: AIChipBench: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Automated AI Accelerator Design
entry.summary: A benchmark asking what LLM coding agents need to write correct hardware: agents implement quantized Qwen3.5, Gemma 3, Gemma 4, and Llama 3.2 decoders in synthesizable RTL against an executable integer reference. It highlights that a wrong decoder state update can pass output tests while corrupting tokens several steps later.

entry.title: Show HN: Comemo – composite memory provider for Hermes Agent

More backends are planned.

entry.title: Research Summary: November 27, 2026
entry.summary: Security dominates this issue: a malicious NPM package (leadstack CRM connect) installed Hermes Agent as root and tasked it remotely over Telegram as a backdoor — best read alongside the Kubernetes write-up showing the official image still requires root at init and ships no Helm chart. On the official side, Hermes Agent now supports Claude Pro/Max subscriptions via a direct SDK plugin (a meaningful change to how users run the agent), and new Kanban documentation formalizes multi-agent profile coordination. Third-party tooling keeps compounding: Comemo works around the single external memory-provider slot by fanning out writes to multiple backends, Hermes-Voice connects agent profiles to Home Assistant Assist, and community friction with agent complexity is spawning both lighter alternatives (shoebox) and orchestration layers built on top (Verso). Practical impact rounds out the section with a reusable VPS + rooted-Android deployment pattern, Apple Silicon throughput gains from agent-written custom kernels over MLX, the venture-backed Almanac launch as ecosystem validation, and research coverage via AIChipBench (LLM agents writing synthesizable RTL). Four promotional SEO listicles were excluded as off-topic.

entry.title: AIChipBench: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Automated AI Accelerator Design
entry.summary: Benchmark evaluating LLM coding agents on implementing quantized decoders (Qwen3.5, Gemma 3, Gemma 4, Llama 3.2) in synthesizable RTL code. entry.title: CARE-3D: Reinforcement Learning for Evidence Grounded Agentic Reasoning in Situated 3D Scenes
entry.summary: Research paper on reinforcement learning for embodied agents performing situated 3D reasoning. It argues existing methods imitate supervised evidence-acquisition traces rather than optimizing how well returned evidence supports correct answers, and that outcome rewards give little credit for intermediate tool choices, leaving rare tools underexplored. CARE-3D addresses credit assignment for evidence gathering in 3D scenes with viewpoint-dependent spatial relations.

entry.summary: Research paper introducing MemOnce, a memory architecture for LLMs in long-horizon and continual interactions. It addresses the tradeoff between standard Transformers, whose token-level KV caches grow linearly in memory and quadratically in compute as context expands, and linear-time architectures that compress history into fixed-size states but lose fine-grained detail. MemOnce maintains reusable memory states for future inference.

entry.title: DailySafe: Benchmarking Dynamic Safety Awareness in Everyday Multi-Turn Multimodal Interactions
entry.summary: Paper presenting DailySafe, a benchmark for evaluating dynamic safety awareness of multimodal LLMs in everyday multi-turn interactions. It critiques existing safety benchmarks for focusing on isolated harmful or adversarial requests while missing risks that emerge as ordinary multi-turn, multimodal tasks unfold, where benign requests can drift into unsafe territory.
